result.markdown: --- title: "[Graph.complement()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Return the complement of the graph. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/edgecase/blob/main/python/edgecase/graph.py#L11732-L11834){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python Graph.complement() ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Creates a new graph with the same nodes but complementary edges. An edge exists in the complement if and only if it does *not* exist in the original graph. Self-loops are never included. New edges have no attributes and default weight (`1.0` for weighted graphs). For directed graphs, complements directed edges independently in each direction. For undirected graphs, complements undirected edges. ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Graph]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A new Graph with complementary edge set. ::: ## Examples {.doc-examples} Complement of a simple graph: ::: {#14bc9ed6 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import edgecase as ec graph = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") ) comp = graph.complement() # Returns 2 (A-C and B-C) comp.count_edges() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` 2 ``` ::: ::: ::: {#64d7701c .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns True comp.has_edge("A", "C") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` True ``` ::: ::: ::: {#34a1aeae .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Returns False (was in original) comp.has_edge("A", "B") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ``` False ``` ::: ::: Finding missing connections in a network: ::: {#f3bad6ea .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Social network with some friendships friends = ( ec.Graph(directed=False) .add_node(label="Alice") .add_node(label="Bob") .add_node(label="Charlie") .add_node(label="Diana") .add_edge("Alice", "Bob") .add_edge("Bob", "Charlie") ) # Find all non-friend pairs (potential connections) non_friends = friends.complement() # Contains: Alice-Charlie, Alice-Diana, Bob-Diana, Charlie-Diana ``` ::: Use in graph theory analysis: ::: {#413a66ec .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Check if graph is self-complementary g = ec.Graph(directed=False) g.add_node(label="A") g.add_node(label="B") g.add_node(label="C") g.add_node(label="D") g.add_edge("A", "B") g.add_edge("C", "D") comp = g.complement() # comp has edges: A-C, A-D, B-C, B-D # Can test if `g` and `comp` are isomorphic ``` ::: Directed graph complement: ::: {#c4a562d5 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} # Directed graph g = ( ec.Graph(directed=True) .add_node(label="A") .add_node(label="B") .add_node(label="C") .add_edge("A", "B") ) comp = g.complement() # `comp` has directed edges: A->C, B->A, B->C, C->A, C->B # (all edges except A->B) ``` :::
